subject.title: 2026.7.1 gateway crash-loop: legacy memory sidecar `meta`/`chunks` conflicts are fatal while `files` conflicts auto-resolve

question: When a legacy Memory Core sidecar has the same row identities as the per-agent database but different values, which state should control startup and how should potentially divergent chunks be preserved?
rationale: Source proves the outage, but changing fail-closed behavior requires an explicit authority and data-preservation policy: metadata/cache drift is derived, while blanket treatment of chunk conflicts could conceal meaningful divergence.

options.title: Canonical DB plus quarantine
options.body: Use canonical rows for runtime, preserve the entire conflicting sidecar under a recoverable timestamped archive, emit a notice, and allow startup to continue.

options.title: Split by table semantics
options.body: Auto-resolve only derived metadata and cache conflicts while keeping divergent chunks blocking until a dedicated reconciliation rule exists.

options.title: Keep fail-closed with real repair
options.body: Retain blocking conflicts but make `openclaw doctor --fix` present and execute a safe canonical-or-legacy recovery choice instead of repeating an unrepairable warning.

recommendation.title: Canonical DB plus quarantine
recommendation.body: Use canonical rows for runtime, preserve the entire conflicting sidecar under a recoverable timestamped archive, emit a notice, and allow startup to continue.

likelyOwner.reason: The broad migration convergence commit most directly frames the unresolved distinction between safely superseded residue and genuinely divergent state.
